questions.q: Describe the themes and techniques of prehistoric rock paintings in India.
answer: Prehistoric rock paintings are the earliest surviving art of India, found on the walls of caves and rock shelters.

answer.text: The paintings mainly depict the life of early people. Common subjects are wild animals such as bison, elephants, tigers and deer, and lively scenes of hunting, dancing, food gathering and riding. Both human and animal figures are shown, often full of movement and energy.

The artists used natural mineral colours, chiefly red obtained from haematite, along with white, and sometimes green and yellow. Red and white were the most common. Brushes were made from plant fibre, and figures were sometimes drawn one over another over long periods.
The finest examples are at Bhimbetka in Madhya Pradesh, a World Heritage Site with hundreds of painted shelters.

answer: These paintings give a vivid picture of early human life.
